entries.summary: Bearish skew unchanged. Reuters reports Brent settlement $96.57 and WTI $84.84 at 13:21 ET, not a settlement. Holiday futures relief remains unconfirmed by cash trading.
bullish: QQQ recovered 3.73 percentage points from morning observation.
Russell 2000 and Dow closed higher; reported 10Y yield fell.
Equal-weight RSP gained 0.78% while SPY fell 0.30% in a secondary closing report.
FT and WSJ report Asian technology-heavy markets rebounding Thursday; proposed tariffs may replace existing levies rather than stack.
IBD reports Nasdaq-100 futures +1.05% versus S&P futures +0.7% overnight; exact quote time unavailable.
IBD reports both NQ and ES futures up 0.55%; holiday relief persists.
FT reports ASML +2.5% and Stoxx 600 +1.5% Thursday, indicating overseas technology relief.
Reuters reports both Nasdaq and S&P futures approximately +0.7%; Barron's reports +0.7% and +0.8% respectively, exact quote times unavailable.
bearish: QQQ lagged SPY by 0.36 percentage points at close.
Reuters reports semiconductor and AI credit stress; VIX rose despite recovery.
SMH reportedly lost 8% over five sessions; secondary SOX report indicates severe weakness, exact timestamp unavailable.
Oil supply disruption risk is corroborated by Reuters; inflation sensitivity remains elevated.
Curated core PCE 3.3% versus 3.2% consensus and GDP 4.3% versus 3.6% forecast reinforce tightening risk; tariff proposals are not yet effective.
S&P CreditWatch Negative on Nvidia AA rating adds financing/governance risk; no downgrade or isolated price reaction confirmed.
IBD reports Micron down 4.5% Wednesday; latest reported NQ futures no longer outperform ES.
Reuters reports China reserves the right to respond to tariffs; Korean chipmakers pared early gains according to FT.
Reuters reports Brent $96.25 and WTI $84.78 after renewed reported Middle East supply disruptions; WSJ independently corroborates rising oil. Exact quote times unavailable.

editorial.marketOverview: US cash and bond markets remain closed for Thanksgiving. Reuters reports Brent settled at $96.57 and WTI traded at $84.84 at 13:21 ET without settlement. Overseas equity gains and earlier positive US futures indicate relief potential, not fresh cash confirmation.
editorial.whatChanged: Brent settlement is only $0.09 above the previous reported quote; WTI is $0.13 above the previous report. These are not synchronized returns. Open Watch metadata refreshed with 181 events and unchanged leading catalysts. No material change.
editorial.marketInterpretation: Elevated crude maintains inflation and valuation risk, while inventory growth and possible unchanged OPEC+ targets temper the supply shock. Reuters reports tariff proposals may not stack on existing July levies, supporting relief. Prior semiconductor weakness, restrictive Fed pricing and lagged positive Treasury curve remain relevant; no new synchronized readings.
editorial.threeDayPath: Friday November 27: early close and thin liquidity favor a possible bounce with fade risk. Monday November 30: normal liquidity and weekend OPEC+ outcome may determine whether oil pressure persists. Tuesday December 1: JOLTS and tentative chip earnings may redirect the rate and semiconductor narrative.
editorial.bullCase: Oil retreat toward $94 alongside broad QQQ participation and SOX outperformance could invalidate the bearish tilt. Overseas equity recovery and prior intraday buying show potential for relief.
editorial.bearCase: Persistent crude strength, restrictive Fed expectations and weak semiconductor leadership could undermine a Friday bounce. Tariff and AI financing uncertainty remain risks, but no new cash equity response has been observed.
editorial.watchNext: Check futures after 18:00 ET reopening, Friday cash breadth, SOX relative strength, VXN/VIX and paired yields. Monitor Sunday OPEC+ and Tuesday JOLTS; issuer earnings dates remain unconfirmed. Compare like-for-like oil contracts around expiry.
